title: Lanes and integration owners: many agents, one shared surface
summary: Drake runs many agents in parallel, each in its own clone or git worktree on its own branch. Every shared surface has exactly one integration owner who merges committed branches only, never touches another agent's dirty tree, and on a conflict aborts and sends it back to the lane that owns the change. I can run a throwaway git demo with four lanes, a clean merge, and a detected conflict.
goal: Run parallel agents without corrupting each other's work, with one owner merging each shared surface.
key_steps: Give every lane its own worktree or clone and branch
Never checkout, reset, stash or clean in another agent's tree
Hand the integration owner committed branches only
On a conflict, abort the merge and keep the shared branch clean
Send the conflict back to the lane, which rebases in its own tree
Merge again and run the combined check

example.code: The host script for this lesson was retired (Part of https://github.com/aien-dev/sovereign-intelligence/issues/31). Read POINTER.md in the example directory. Where this lesson has Omega sources, they are listed there. Where it was a tree inspection or a git demo, the recorded output is the evidence.
example.output:
worktree lane-a rc=0
worktree lane-b rc=0
worktree lane-c rc=0
worktree lane-d rc=0

== lanes work in parallel, each in its own tree
lane-a commit rc=0
lane-b commit rc=0
lane-b leaves an uncommitted file: ?? wip.txt

== integration owner merges committed branches only
merge lane-a rc=0
merge lane-b rc=0
main now has: docs.txt parser.txt shared.txt 
lane-b uncommitted file on main: absent
lane-b dirty tree untouched: ?? wip.txt

== two lanes edit the same line of a shared file
lane-c commit rc=0
lane-d commit rc=0
merge lane-c rc=0
merge lane-d rc=1
conflicted files: shared.txt
owner aborts the merge rc=0, main is clean: []
CONFLICT: lane-d must rebase onto main in its own worktree and re-decide shared.txt

== lane d resolves in its own tree, owner merges again
lane-d rebase rc=1 (conflict expected)
lane-d rebase --continue rc=0
merge lane-d rc=0
final shared.txt:
owner: integration
version: 3 (lane d, after lane c)
main history:
  merge lane-d
  merge lane-c
  merge lane-b
  merge lane-a
  base

common_mistake: 'Helping' in a shared checkout with git stash or checkout, destroying someone's uncommitted work, or resolving a conflict on the shared branch by picking a side. Fix: isolated worktrees, and conflicts go back to the lane that knows its change.
evidence_note: The example ran on a Linux AArch64 host (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte with a negative control. Rests on the recorded git run in a throwaway repository: two clean merges, the uncommitted file left untouched, a detected conflict (merge rc=1) aborted cleanly, then resolved in the lane. NOT done: this is a mechanics demo, not a measured multi-agent session.
